candidates.reason: TIMER-SIDE: xprt_init_autodisconnect (def net/sunrpc/xprt.c:697-714) is registered via setup_timer(&xprt->timer, xprt_init_autodisconnect, ...) at xprt.c:1375 and takes plain spin_lock(&xprt->transport_lock) at line 702 (unlock 709/713); plain acquisition is acceptable from TIMER_SOFTIRQ context. HOLDER-SIDE VERIFIED: every other acquisition of xprt->transport_lock in xprt.c uses spin_lock_bh/spin_unlock_bh (275/277, 381/383, 516/522, 599/601, 631/634, 646/652, 669/680, 722/731, 737/746, 900/906, 922/942, 970/976, 995/1020, 1289/1297), including the workqueue worker xprt_autoclose (INIT_WORK(&xprt->task_cleanup, xprt_autoclose) at 1373; body locks at 631/646/669) that the timer callback itself queues via queue_work(xprtiod_workqueue, &xprt->task_cleanup) at line 710. The process/workqueue holder side always disables bottom halves, so a TIMER softirq on the same CPU cannot spin against a plain holder that can never resume - the missing-BH invariant is satisfied for this lock within xprt.c. Residual gap: whether net/sunrpc/sock_xprt.c or net/sunrpc/xprtrdma add plain process-context transport_lock sites was not verified (the two grep attempts failed on cwd and rg permission before the search halt).

limitations: Bounded negative result: the scripted enumeration in this session scanned 16,667 .c files under drivers/, net/, kernel/, mm/, fs/, block/, ipc/, security/ and lib/, matched 741 distinct timer callback names registered via timer_setup/setup_timer/DEFINE_TIMER/init_timer, and body-scanned those callbacks for plain spin_lock - exactly one hit (net/sunrpc/xprt.c xprt_init_autodisconnect:702), which was triaged safe. No timer_list callback with a violated missing-BH invariant was confirmed in s03.

Enumeration gap: the function-body extraction only matched definitions whose function name begins a line (K&R split style, e.g. 'static void\nfoo(unsigned long data)\n{'); single-line definitions such as 'static void br_multicast_group_expired(struct timer_list *t) {' were not body-scanned, so an unknown fraction of timer callbacks (including the known br_multicast and libiscsi bug families) were never enumerated in s03.

hrtimer handlers (hrtimer_init + .function assignment), timers registered via indirect function pointers or struct initializers, and trees outside the scanned roots (arch/, sound/, crypto/, virt/, samples/, tools/) were not enumerated; delayed_work expiry was not separately covered (the dwork timer softirq only queues the work; the user callback itself runs in worker/process context).

net/bridge/br_multicast.c (br->multicast_lock) and drivers/scsi/libiscsi.c (session->frwd_lock) are confirmed vulnerable shapes in sibling snapshots s07 and s05 at the same paths; their s03 copies remain unverified and are the highest-priority follow-up for the timer-dwork-softirq-lock branch on this snapshot.

The xprt transport_lock analysis covered xprt.c only; possible plain process-context acquisitions in net/sunrpc/sock_xprt.c and net/sunrpc/xprtrdma/ sharing the same lock object were not checked (both grep attempts failed on cwd/rg-permission before the halt).
Static source analysis only: no build, lockdep run or runtime reproducer was performed (the snapshot tree lacks .config and generated headers).

The staging ks7010 seed bug present in s03 (drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c:374 per the prior s03 xmit-branch pass) is xmit-shaped, not timer-shaped, and is excluded from reporting in any case per the never-report-the-seed rule.
